answer: When agents register they each submit a cryptographic proof bound to a unique hardware enclave that emits a continuous low‑entropy beacon, forming a velvet‑soft timing prism the network monitors. The ledger groups any identities whose beacons share a synchronized edge, placing them on a shared ledge of a payment‑vault contract that requires a separate stake for each group. An attacker must acquire multiple independent enclaves and fund each stake, raising the cost linearly with the number of forged identities.
